papers.title: StatefulDiscovery: Evidence-Calibrated Claim Formation in Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
papers.gap: Stateful claim formation couples executed-analysis evidence with claim confidence and frontier control for open-ended data discovery; it does not adjudicate literature relations entering a shared knowledge graph: no character-span provenance, no graph admission states (accepted/needs_review/rejected), no evidence-event revision (add/delete/refute/supersede) with replay, and no human-override event.

papers.title: Reliable Post-Retrieval Assembly for Agent Memory: Separating Evidence Extraction from Policy Execution
papers.venue: arXiv preprint (accepted, Lifelong Agent Workshop at COLM 2026)
papers.gap: Separating evidence extraction from deterministic policy execution fixes memory conflict assembly and shows LLM-mediated freshness tracking is the bottleneck; it handles versioned facts with an explicit total order, not scientific relations whose evidence sufficiency, semantic strength, calibrated risk, and human override must be adjudicated before graph admission.
